candidate_solve.assumed_parameters_from_coaching_figure: Geometric configuration of S, C, ACB in vertical plane with downward gravity.
candidate_solve.derivation: Bead Q traverses straight chord AB of length 2R with uniform horizontal velocity v: t_Q = 2R/v. Bead P traverses curved semi-circular wire ACB. Under gravity, as P descends below AB, mechanical energy conservation gives v_P(theta) = sqrt(v_0^2 + 2gy) > v. However, the path length is pi*R approx 3.14 R, whereas AB is 2R. Whether t_P < t_Q depends on the exact initial point S, the ratio v^2/(gR), and whether the horizontal velocity component remains greater than v throughout. In the coaching solution, t_P < t_Q (Option A) is asserted based on average horizontal speed enhancement, but without the exact figure and rigorous bound, the result cannot be conclusively certified.
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If g -> 0, path ACB is longer (pi*R > 2R) with constant speed v, so t_P = pi*R/v > 2R/v = t_Q. If g is very large, descent velocity becomes extremely high, driving t_P -> 0, so t_P < t_Q. Crossover depends sensitively on v^2/(gR).

sl2.crux: Analyzing the trade-off between increased path length along a circular arc versus increased speed from gravitational potential energy conversion.
